rationale: The attribution rule for R has exactly one moving part, and this fixture is where it is pinned. `lapply(items, function(item) transform_one(item))` calls `transform_one` from inside an ANONYMOUS function, so the nearest enclosing NAMED binding is `outer` -- not `item`, which is a parameter and not a symbol, and not `global`, which has no body to attribute to. The confidence is pinned to EXACTLY 0.7 with a max as well as a min: 55.6% of R call sites in the corpus sit at file scope with no enclosing named symbol at all, and those are counted in `metadata.callAttribution.unresolvedScope` rather than given an invented source. A call whose only home is a parameter name is forbidden three ways, because publishing `outer -> item` puts a name in the graph that R never binds at any scope. `local({ nested() })` is here for the opposite reason: `nested` is at 1.0, because `local()` creates no `function_definition` node, and F14 pins that its assignments do not become file-level bindings.
